honestyNote: Filed after the first live reads rather than before them (this lane ran as one pass). The falsifiers and the counting rules below were fixed before the measurements that decide them; the two divergence findings moved nothing in this list, they were the pre-registered questions answered.

in: Establish, per rail (parcelGeometry, pipelines, railCorridor, etjStatus, landUseDescription): the exact serve path today (service, function, store or upstream), the ledger cell state (empty / partially written / written-and-unread), the concrete cutover cost (which writer mints the atoms, population, any vocabulary or contract change), what breaks if it never cuts over, and a recommendation (CUT OVER | STAYS ELSEWHERE | RETIRE) with the serve path named.
Prove at least two serve paths by violation (a read that fails or a value that disappears when the path is unavailable).
One ruling table plus one paragraph on which rails are ruled together and which needs its own decision.
out: No store writes of any kind. No deploys. No serving changes. No edits to RAIL_POLICY (adding an accept list is what IMPLEMENTS a ruling; the ruling has not been made).
County 48491 not touched in any store (no read, no write).
No sub-agents (FAN-DEPTH 0). This lane does the work itself.
No change to six-county-completeness.mjs or any enforcement script.
scope.whyTheseBoundaries: The dispatch's mission is a ruling input, not a build: the five rails are open only because no accept list exists for the class, and every one of them was believed to serve already. So the deliverable is facts plus a recommendation, and any implementation (an accept list, a writer, a panel fix) is downstream of an operator ruling. The exclusions above are the dispatch's own constraints; adding any of them would have turned a $0 read-only lane into a serving change and made the ruling's premise untestable.

preRegisteredFalsifiers.statement: If the named read is what serves a rail, removing the thing it reads removes the served value (or produces a typed refusal) — and adding it produces the value.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.predicted: parcelGeometry and pipelines PASS (atom counts will track the served output exactly); any rail whose served value survives with its store empty is NOT served by that read.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.band: an exact match between atom count and served edge count on every parcel sampled; no tolerated drift.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.howTested: ablation by subject: parcels chosen to span 0 and n atoms, then both ends read live.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.result: confirmed for parcelGeometry (9/9, 12/12, 5/5, 7/7, and refused on 0) and pipelines (true/false with distance and operator from the atom body).

preRegisteredFalsifiers.statement: If the ledger is the serving path for a rail, a served value must be traceable to that rail's cell (atom reference / render key), not to a bake or a serve-time computation.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.predicted: for these five rails the cell is EMPTY in all six counties and the served value comes from somewhere else; if any rail's served value is atom-backed and cell-less, the cell is accounting-only and the cutover is cheap.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.howTested: read the served payload's own rail-state map (recordRailStates) and the atomic provenance blocks on each fact (provenanceClass / serveLayer), and read the completeness instrument's cell-facing output.
preRegisteredFalsifiers.result: recordRailStates carries none of the five rails and reports atomBacked:false on every key it does carry; the fact blocks carry atom provenance (Record/Derivation) while the cells stay excluded-mid-cutover.
